Avalon Global Asset Management Has Lifted Its Position in Stanley Black & Decker (SWK) as Share Value Declined; Public Sector Pension Investment Board Cut Public Svc Enterprise Group (PEG) Stake by $6.38 Million as Share Value Declined
May 11, 2018 - By Winifred Garcia
Avalon Global Asset Management Llc increased its stake in Stanley Black & Decker Inc (SWK) by 100% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Avalon Global Asset Management Llc bought 15,000 shares as the company’s stock declined 8.99% with the market. The hedge fund held 30,000 shares of the capital goods company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $5.09M, up from 15,000 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Avalon Global Asset Management Llc who had been investing in Stanley Black & Decker Inc for a number of months, seems to be bullish on the $22.16 billion market cap company. The stock increased 0.31% or $0.45 during the last trading session, reaching $143.59. About 60,829 shares traded. Stanley Black & Decker, Inc. (NYSE:SWK) has risen 16.50% since May 11, 2017 and is uptrending. It has outperformed by 4.95% the S&P500.
Public Sector Pension Investment Board decreased its stake in Public Svc Enterprise Group (PEG) by 82.42% based on its latest 2017Q4 regulatory filing with the SEC. Public Sector Pension Investment Board sold 125,000 shares as the company’s stock declined 3.43% with the market. The institutional investor held 26,666 shares of the power generation company at the end of 2017Q4, valued at $1.37M, down from 151,666 at the end of the previous reported quarter. Public Sector Pension Investment Board who had been investing in Public Svc Enterprise Group for a number of months, seems to be less bullish one the $25.84B market cap company.
